articles.headline: Bengals' chances of making playoffs look interesting at bye
keyFacts: ESPN's Football Power Index gives the Cincinnati Bengals a 76 percent chance to make the NFL playoffs at their bye week.
The 3-2 Bengals face remaining opponents with losing records including the Tennessee Titans, Washington, and New Orleans.
The Bengals return from their bye week to play the Baltimore Ravens.
body: The Cincinnati Bengals appear to be in the driver’s seat on the way to a playoff spot.
It’s early, but most projections at the bye week still have the Bengals taking care of business against some soft parts of their schedule to wrap up a playoff spot this winter.
Take ESPN's Football Power Index , which still gives the Bengals a 76 percent chance to make the playoffs after running simulations. Only a 33 percent chance to win the AFC North, but alas.
Currently on a bye week, the Bengals will need to exit it and pick up a win over the Baltimore Ravens before getting a soft 0-5 Tennessee team.
The Bengals also have 1-3-1 Washington, 1-4 New Orleans, 2-2 Carolina and 2-3 Indianapolis still on the schedule.

If the Bengals can take care of teams that are supposedly worse than them, they only lost in Pittsburgh by three in Week 3. That rematch, plus four other AFC North games, give them a strong shot at the postseason.

Lots of ifs in there, like better linebacker play, better safety play, finding running game success and staying healthy, yes. But the Bengals, despite being a mildly disappointing 3-2 at the break, look just fine.

articles.headline: The New Street Fighter Movie Gets Savaged By Critics, But Not Everyone Hates It
keyFacts: The new live-action Street Fighter movie has opened to negative reviews and a 41 percent score on Rotten Tomatoes.
Critics described the film as an incoherent mess with confusing jokes, though some praised its action sequences and entertainment value.
The movie is scheduled to release in theaters starting October 16.
body: A celebrity-filled cast. A director best known for his work on the Eric Andre show. One of the most iconic and beloved franchises in gaming. What could go wrong? Apparently quite a lot. The Street Fighter movie is getting panned by many critics. Not quite as bad as 2024’s Borderlands adaptation, but still very far from great.

Starring Noah Centineo as Ken Masters, Andrew Koji as Ryu, and Callina Liang as Chun-Li, Hollywood’s latest attempt to cash in on Capcom’s longrunning fighting game series marketed itself from the jump as a very silly affair. Cody Rhodes looks absurd as Guile. 50 Cent is playing Balrog. They even let Eric AndrÃ© on screen as ring announcer Don Sauvage. But based on early reviews, unlike Mortal Kombat 2, which committed to its dumb premise with unflinching B-action movie conviction, Street Fighter sounds like a dizzying mess of abbreviated character arcs and humor that doesn’t land.

Officially in theaters starting October 16, the live-action adaptation has opened to a 41 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. That’s even lower than A Minecraft Movie, which was completely unwatchable. Some reviews have accused director Kitao Sakurai’s take on Street Fighter of being an “incoherent, irredeemable mess” and “dumber than a box of rocks.” TheWrap slammed its 1990s nostalgia-fest as anachronistic and suffering from “cultural collapse.” The nicest thing Variety had to say about it was that the dialogue was often inaudible due to the “thundering sound mix.”

Not everyone was appalled. IndieWire applauded Street Fighter for at least not being boring, while The New York Times praised it as the sort of thing a kid who lost all their pocket change to Street Fighter in the arcade might begin to hallucinate in their dreams. Here’s what else the early reviews are saying:

[The film] overflows with convoluted plotting and confusingly engineered jokes. But a filmâs greatest sin is boring its audience, and this “Street Fighterâ should take pride in never coming close to doing that. Fans of the âStreet Fighterâ games donât spend much time thinking about the overarching lore. The games are a flashy vessel to project yourself onto while you play with martial artists, each with their own unique aesthetics. And at the end of the day, this movie delivers the same thing. Itâs a blank emotional canvas whose value lies in what you make of it â but it sure looks cool as hell. – Christian Zilko

Most importantly, the film is dedicated to the punchy pyrotechnics of its fight sequences, most of which are constructed to feature the diverse personalities of its many fighters. This can eventually seem like a weakness, as the film tries to flit between one too many showdowns, tiring viewers out while confusing them on the movieâs priorities. But in another sense, it simply feels like the natural zenith of an arcade playerâs imagination, the âand then, and thenâ output of fighter fantasies running wild. By the end, you can practically see the â90s kid smashing and kicking at the air on his way out of the theater. – Brandon Yu

David Dastmalchianâs eyes roll back as he presses his thumbs into a sniveling scientistâs eye sockets. As the skull cracks and blood splatters across Dastmalchian’s forehead, he makes an expression that can be best described as orgasm face. This happens within the first 10 minutes of Street Fighter, in which Dastmalchian plays the fighting game franchiseâs chief antagonist, M. Bison. Itâs a perfect performance â a masterclass in B-movie camp. Unfortunately, nobody else in Street Fighter is anywhere close to operating on Dastmalchianâs level. To make matters worse, not even writer-director Kitao Sakurai seems to know what kind of movie heâs making, leading to one of the sloppiest, cringiest, and most incoherent films of the year. – Jake Kleinman

Whenever Ken or Ryu start emoting or waxing philosophical like Steven Seagal or Van Damme in those movies that inspire Street Fighter, Liangâs Chun-Li calls out in the most basic terms how stupid they sound. Thereâs several knowing winks at the fans like this, guarding against criticism by owning up to how silly this all is, which would land better if the movie ever rose above the stuff itâs making fun of. Instead, Street Fighter is satisfied punching down on itself, and everything thatâs cringe about the 90s, while happily being stuck there, in the past, so it could pretend that this is as good as it gets for video game adaptations. – Radheyan Simonpillai

Street Fighter is dumber than a box of rocks, but have you ever thrown rocks at things? It can be pretty fun with the right combination of enthusiastic friends and anarchic spirit. Kitao Sakurai doesnât always succeed in marshalling his enthusiastic cast and anarchic approach to the filmâs blend of action and comedy, with too many characters there to service too thin a story, but Street Fighterâs all about landing as many punches as it can before the round timer hits zero.Â Even though there are plenty of misses, the ones it does manage to land hit hard. – Tom Jorgensen

As the film becomes increasingly split between the tournament and M. Bisonâs unraveling conspiracy, something goes terribly awry in its back half, hinting at either a troubled production, or one that was doomed from the start. The dialogue, whether expository exchanges or quippy one-liners, grows splintered, and is increasingly presented with the backs of speakersâ heads or their mouths partially obscured; it would be interesting to learn how much of the film was rewritten in post. – Siddhant Adlakha

Some fans may break out their torches and pitchforks, but I for one embrace this Frankenstein monster. Itâs so oblivious to narrative and stylistic cohesion that itâs almost spiritual. Watching âStreet Fighterâ is to exist outside time itself. Thatâs my theory and Iâm sticking to it, because otherwise thereâs no explanation for why this film begins in 1987 with Ryu listening to âWhatâs Upâ by 4 Non Blondes on his walkman, a song which wouldnât come out for another six years. When the action leaps ahead to 1993, Kenâs manager proudly declares that Taco Bell is going to name a Gordita after him, even though Taco Bell wouldnât add the Gordita to their menu until a half decade later. – William Bibbiani

“Street Fighter” is a highly watchable movie, and it’s not too hard to convince yourself you’re having fun while seeing it. Yet its aftertaste is so bitter and its center so hollow that it’s hard to recommend, and certainly not as an introduction to this world. There may be enough in the film’s attract mode to get me to press start, but I ended up not wanting to continue.” – Bill Bria

articles.headline: At least 4, including 3 children, killed in US elementary school shooting
keyFacts: Four people, including three children, were killed in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, according to law enforcement.
Bend Police Department officials said the suspect is dead and officers are currently going room by room to evacuate people from the school.
The FBI and Oregon Governor Tina Kotek stated that they are monitoring the situation and assisting local law enforcement with the investigation.
body: At least four people have been killed, including three children, in a shooting at an elementary school in Oregon, part of the northwestern United States, according to statements from law enforcement to CBS and CNN.
The shooting on Thursday took place at Silver Rail Elementary school in the city of Bend, about 160km (100 miles) southeast of Portland.
Authorities have said the shooter is dead, though it is unclear whether he is among the four people included in the initial death toll.

“We’re in the process at this time of going room by room and evacuating each of the people who are in that school,” said Sheila Miller, the communications manager for the Bend Police Department on Thursday. “This is the kind of thing we never want to see happen in Bend. It’s devastating.”
Miller said authorities received a call about a shot fired into a car outside the school at 12:59pm local time (19:59 GMT) and arrived on scene within minutes.
The suspect was shot and killed shortly after, though Miller said she did not know whether police or a bystander had subdued the alleged assailant.
The number and condition of those injured were not immediately known.
Kash Patel, the director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), said in a post on social media that the agency was on the scene assisting local law enforcement in the investigation.
“We will make every resource they need available,” he wrote.
Oregon Governor Tina Kotek also said she was closely monitoring the situation.
Jeff Merkley, who represents Oregon in the US Senate, was among the political leaders to offer condolences in the wake of the shooting.
“My heart is with the Bend community and all of the students and families affected. No one should have to fear violence at school,” he wrote in a post on the social media platform X.

articles.headline: GOP hawks urge Trump to force Putin to make a deal: ‘Need a Churchill’
keyFacts: Republican hawks and former national security officials are urging President Trump to use stricter pressure against Russian President Vladimir Putin to force a peace deal.
Lawmakers and critics warned that lifting sanctions on Russian diesel and restricting military capabilities for Kyiv risk aiding Russia's war in Ukraine.
Tensions between the US and Ukraine escalated as Ukrainian forces resumed refinery strikes and faced interruptions in US-facilitated internet services.
body: WASHINGTON — Republican hawks and former national security officials are urging President Trump to force Russian President Vladimir Putin back to the negotiating table by using sticks instead of carrots.

The president’s critics warn that suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports, alienating Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and restricting some military capabilities for Kyiv are tantamount to greenlighting Putin’s war against Ukraine.
“Our President has become Neville Chamberlain,” wrote Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.) in a post on X, referring to the former British prime minister who practiced appeasement with Adolf Hitler.

The stepped-up calls come after renewed Ukrainian attacks on refineries ended a brief energy cease-fire and interruptions in US-provided internet services for Ukraine’s military sparked panic on the battlefield.

“We need peace, but it has to be on terms that demonstrate that you can’t have a power like Vladimir Putin rolling through a European nation,” Mike Pompeo, who served as secretary of state and CIA director during Trump’s first term, said on Fox Business.

“I’ve seen the reports on this Starlink issue. We should make sure that we are providing all the stuff that the Ukrainians need to put pressure on Russia, so they can continue their long-range strikes,” he added.

House and Senate lawmakers have been pressing Trump to get tougher with Russia, rather than Ukraine, and focus on implementing sanctions passed in a bill named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC) as a tactic toward peace.

“Putin has repeatedly shown that he responds to pressure, not goodwill,” wrote Rep. Michael McCaul (R-Texas) in a bipartisan letter to the president Thursday. “With the October 18 deadline approaching, we again urge you to implement this law fully and faithfully.”
McCaul told The Post Thursday that he was “concerned the recent lifting of sanctions on Russian oil will only fuel the Kremlin’s violence and destruction.”

“In fact, we have already seen Vladimir Putin’s response: continued bombardment of Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, even after President Trump called for an energy ceasefire. Meanwhile, Russian forces have carried out indiscriminate strikes on civilian targets — injuring and murdering buses full of innocent people, in violation of international law,” McCaul said.
“Putin’s disdain for peace couldn’t be clearer. A full and faithful implementation of our bill is required to cripple his war machine and finally bring him to the negotiating table.”
On Thursday, it appeared US-Ukraine relations had sunk to a new low, as Zelensky openly flouted Trump’s Sunday announcement of a limited truce pertaining to oil facilities.
“The block is out. We’re done,” Zelensky said to the Financial Times during a trip to London after Russia struck Ukrainian power infrastructure.

Ukrainian drones hit a refinery about 180 miles southeast of Moscow on Thursday — defying Trump, who has for weeks unsuccessfully urged the Ukrainian leader to cease attacks on Russian refineries due to their impact on oil and diesel prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm election.

Ukraine said this week it did not receive advance intelligence from the US of incoming Russian attacks and that its military has had interruptions in US-facilitated Starshield internet services, a military version of Starlink used for battlefield and drone operations.
Elon Musk, whose company operates the service, said Wednesday that “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.”

Trump on Tuesday denied breaking off routine intelligence sharing with Ukraine and on Thursday two administration officials denied that the president had ordered a throttling of internet services — leaving both matters murky against a clear backdrop of tension with Kyiv.

Four Senate Republicans — Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, John Cornyn of Texas and Tom Tillis of North Carolina — signed onto a letter Thursday from Sen. Jeanne Shaheen’s (D-NH) asking Pentagon inspector general Platte Moring to probe the cause of the internet slowdown.
Ukraine’s Charge D’Affaires Denys Sienik said Thursday that “Star Shield speeds have been improved, at the moment. We hope all will be resumed to the previous level.”

“Speed is critical for logistics, and for intercepting the jet-powered Shahed drones especially when Russia constantly uses them to attack our cities and commit war crimes and when Foreign Minister Lavrov openly states that Russia opposes a ceasefire,” added Sienik.

The Pentagon didn’t respond to requests for comment. A source familiar with the speed restrictions said that “one of the most massive Shahed attacks, occurring precisely when our defense system’s speed was being throttled, and the circumstances behind this are deeply concerning.”

“Ultimately, I believe the tipping point for a peace deal will come when Putin finally accepts that the war is unwinnable and his only chance for an honorable exit is through a deal with Trump,” said Fred Fleitz, chief of staff of the National Security Council during Trump’s first term.
“This should be the central theme of any [Steve]Witkoff-[Jared] Kushner negotiations with Putin.”
Zelensky’s resumed refinery strikes and the internet interruption are the latest points of strain with the White House after a tumultuous week of developments.

Last Friday, Trump announced that he was waiving US sanctions on Russian diesel in a bid to lower prices that had nearly doubled over the past year, driven by the Russia-Ukraine conflict and his own war with Iran. Putin agreed to lift export restrictions he had imposed last year.

Trump made the move in frustration over Zelensky’s drone attacks on Russian refineries. But the change of tactics designed to entice Putin back to the bargaining table horrified critics who said it could provide $4 billion for Putin’s war effort.

Zelensky ripped the diesel deal as “weak” — with Trump retaliating on Saturday by saying “it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president,” claiming Zelensky “wants to make problems for the world” and “he’d better damn well stop.”

Trump on Sunday announced what he called an “energy cease-fire” between Russia and Ukraine, which Zelensky initially said he would abide by, but publicly stretched the meaning to include all energy targets, whereas the deal only pertained to oil refineries and pumping stations, per a US source.

Zelensky accused Russia of violating the deal by striking natural gas facilities and broke off his participation on Thursday.
Former national security officials in Democratic administrations have also criticized the president’s moves with respect to Ukraine.

“Trump stumbled into an energy crisis due to his unsuccessful Iran war, so he struck a deal for Russian diesel that, ironically, will do little to lower diesel prices but will put money into Putin’s war machine,” said Daniel Shapiro, a former US ambassador to Israel under President Joe Biden.

“And then, when Zelenskyy did not agree to end strikes on Russian diesel facilities, he used the manufactured crisis as an excuse to weaken Ukraine’s defenses against Russian drones and ballistic missiles,” Shapiro added.

“For Trump, it’s a two-fer: try to lower diesel prices to save his own skin before the midterms, and use more Ukrainian deaths to strongarm Zelenskyy to accept a surrender agreement with Russia so Trump can claim to have ended the war. Neither will work.”

articles.headline: Minus 17 to European dreams as Bournemouth fairytale continues
keyFacts: Bournemouth played their first European home game in the club's 127-year history, defeating Sturm Graz 3-0 in the Europa League.
The club overcame administration and a 17-point deduction in League Two in 2008 to reach the Premier League and European competition.
Bournemouth will next play a Premier League match against Sunderland on Sunday before hosting AC Milan next week.
body: - Published
It was a night soundtracked by the Impossible Dream.
And it was no coincidence that was the song chosen at the Vitality Stadium before Bournemouth's first European home game in the club's 127-year history.

As supporters lucky enough to bag a ticket for the historic occasion waved flags to the Andy Williams classic, a giant tifo rose from behind one of the stands, bearing the words 'Minus 17 to European dreams. AFC Bournemouth, established 1899'.
As recently as 2008, a night like this would have been unthinkable for Cherries supporters.
Just 18 years ago, Bournemouth were facing the prospect of no longer existing.
After entering administration, the club were relegated from League One after being handed a 10-point deduction.
But that was not the end of their troubles. To be allowed to compete in the 2008-09 season, Bournemouth, then managed by Eddie Howe, had to accept a further 17-point deduction in League Two.
It left them at the bottom of the Football League and seemingly destined for life as a non-league side.

By the end of the season, the Cherries had not only completed one of the greatest escapes in English football history to secure a 21st-place finish and survival, but had also laid the foundations for a decade of success, which culminated in a first promotion to the Premier League in 2015.

Fast-forward to the present day and Bournemouth are making history for all the right reasons in the Europa League. Thursday's 3-0 win over Sturm Graz meant they became only the second English side to win their first two matches in a major European competition since Bolton achieved the feat in the Uefa Cup 21 years ago.
"It's a moment that will live long in their memories," former defender Joel Ward told TNT Sports. "The club should relish this night.
"The owner [Bill Foley] manifested this moment when he first came into the club. He set the standards for this club, he has invested a lot into it and he wanted to see this club in Europe.
"He got his wish, and they have certainly started incredibly well so far."
Smith embodies Bournemouth's fairytale
It was a night that always seemed destined to produce a fairytale storyline, such has been the nature of Bournemouth's rise since 2008.

At Wednesday's pre-match press conference, defender Adam Smith - the club's longest-serving player after initially joining on loan from Tottenham in 2011 - admitted he would never have imagined captaining the Cherries in Europe.

But there was more to come for Smith. The right-back earned his own piece of history by providing the assist for Bournemouth's first European goal on home soil, with Evanilson heading his cross home late in the first half.
"It's been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it, so we are very happy," Smith told TNT Sports.
"We had a chat with each other and we got a reaction today. That's an AFC [Bournemouth] performance right there."
Since making his move from Tottenham permanent in 2014, Smith has made more than 430 appearances for the Cherries.
In that time, the 35-year-old has helped Bournemouth secure three promotions, two of which have taken them to the Premier League.
When he was replaced by James Hill midway through the second half, the home supporters rose to their feet and chanted Smith's name as he departed the field.
"He's an example to everyone of what hard work looks like and the rewards that you get, even towards the latter stages of your career," added Ward.

"He's extremely professional, and he fully deserves the success he's getting now. Nights like this are what you live for. To walk out captaining that side is emotional and makes the hair stand up on the back of your neck."
'If we stick together and play like this... then we are hard to play against'
It was no surprise to see Bournemouth supporters remain in their seats long after the final whistle as they attempted to soak up as much as they could of a landmark night on the south coast.
For Marco Rose and his players, though, the focus will quickly shift to Sunday's Premier League clash with Sunderland.
Despite soaring to new heights in the Europa League during the opening weeks of the season, their Premier League campaign is yet to get going.
The Cherries sit 18th in the table and are one of only three teams, alongside Fulham and Tottenham, yet to win a match this season.
"If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans, then we are hard to play against and it's hard to beat us," said Rose, who succeeded Andoni Iraola in June.
"That's what we should take into the next game."
Bournemouth's remarkable story will enter arguably its most glamorous chapter yet when AC Milan visit the Vitality Stadium next week.

articles.headline: World Timekeepers Decide to Kill the Leap Second
keyFacts: The General Conference on Weights and Measures voted on Thursday to abolish the leap second.
Officials said the decision prevents future technical disruptions and computer crashes caused by time adjustments.
Continuous UTC will become effective on May 20, 2027, meaning no more leap seconds will be added.
body: Human timekeeping rests on two main clocks, and they don’t always run at the same speed. For decades, the solution was the leap second, a minor adjustment added to international time to keep atomic accuracy aligned with the Earth’s natural motion. But on Thursday, the General Conference on Weights and Measures, or the CGPM (abbreviated from its French name), voted to abolish the leap second, closing a long-standing chapter in global time sync.

Most modern clocks rely on Coordinated Universal Time, a hybrid system caught between atomic time, which flows at a near-perfectly constant rate, and astronomical time, which fluctuates as the Earth’s rotation speeds up and slows down. To bridge the gap, UTC periodically inserted a leap second to keep pace with the planet. But reconciling physical planetary shifts with precise digital systems ultimately created more technical disruptions than it solved.
Breaking time

Computers are sensitive when it comes to timekeeping. The last few times we added a leap second to UTC — in 2012, 2015 and 2016 – some computer systems couldn’t handle it. Of the three instances, 2012 was the worst, as adding a leap second caused issues that crashed websites and software platforms, such as Reddit, LinkedIn and Mozilla.
More from CNET

The speed of Earth’s rotation experiences small changes all the time. While we can’t predict exactly how fast Earth will rotate in the future, the conference wrote that there’s a 30% chance we’ll have to add a negative leap second by 2035 to keep UTC aligned with rotational time.

If adding a regular leap second was trouble, imagine what adding a negative leap second could do. The conference doesn’t want to risk finding out. So, potential future computer anomalies caused by UTC changes are a major reason why the leap second is going away.

“Industrial users and the synchronization needs of national critical infrastructures, for example, transportation, energy distribution, telecommunication, and space projects, require UTC to be continuous without any future adjustment,” the group’s resolution reads.
Moving forward

The official death of the leap second will be May 20, 2027, when continuous UTC becomes effective. A continuous UTC means that no more leap seconds, negative or otherwise, will be added to UTC going forward. This also means that UTC and rotational time will begin to drift apart.
The CGPM noted that allowing time measurements to differ by up to an hour will keep UTC stable for several centuries.

This means in the future, when it’s noon, the sun might not be at its highest in the sky. But, considering we’ve only added 27 leap seconds since the concept was introduced in 1972, any changes that occur within our lifetimes will probably be very small.

articles.headline: Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
keyFacts: A bus carrying lorry drivers hit a stationary freight train at the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel, French authorities said.
French authorities said the bus driver and 18 passengers were injured, with two severely hurt but none facing life-threatening conditions.
French officials stated that tunnel traffic was not disrupted following a brief stoppage, and an investigation into the collision has begun.
body: - Published
A bus has hit a stationary freight train near the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel, injuring the driver and 18 passengers, French authorities say.
The bus, which was carrying lorry drivers due to take a shuttle rail service, struck the train at the loading platform of the tunnel in Coquelles, near Calais, at 19:27 (18:27 BST) on Thursday.
The bus driver and one passenger were severely injured and evacuated by helicopter. None of the injuries were life threatening, a local official said.
Local sub-prefect Agathe Cury said freight and Eurostar passenger traffic through the tunnel had not been disrupted after a brief stoppage to evacuate injured people. An investigation has begun.

"Two trains were on either side of the platform. One was being loaded by heavy goods vehicles ahead of a cross-Channel journey, and another train that had previously been loaded was departing," Cury said.
"For a reason that currently remains unknown, the minibus collided with the departing train.
"The bus did not overturn, it is still upright â but the shock and the collision caused injuries to the people involved."
The incident involved a minibus transporting workers who were about to board Le Shuttle. All were men of different nationalities, she added.
It is not clear whether any British nationals are among the injured.
Cury said it was "the first time an incident of this type has occurred" on an Eurotunnel loading platform.
The BBC's Evan Davis, who was travelling through the Eurotunnel to Calais at the time of the incident, witnessed blue light vehicles "concentrated on one of the platforms" as he entered France.
"There were plenty of cars queueing up at check-in when I drove past just now, and I saw some cars going through check-in, so despite the collision they weren't being held," he said from the scene.
Photos published by local French newspaper La Voix du Nord, external showed a small bus with damage to its front and side standing alongside a train, among a crowd of emergency workers.
Eurostar has released an update saying: "An incident occurred several kilometers away from the Channel Tunnel.
"This incident does not involved or impact Eurostar trains running from and to London. All of Eurostar trains will run as expected."
The Eurotunnel runs under the sea between England and France, from Folkestone in Kent to Coquelles on the French side.

Three different rail services operate through the tunnel - the Eurostar, a passenger train that begins in London and goes to several European destinations, freight trains which transport goods and Le Shuttle, which transports vehicles.

articles.headline: AOC says Trump administration doesn’t want women attending college
keyFacts: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez stated that a Department of Education student loan rule targets women-dominated fields and prevents women from attending college.
The DOE rule requires college programs to prove graduates earn more than non-graduates or face disqualification from federal student loan programs.
The Department of Education dismissed the reports as fake news on X, stating the rule holds colleges accountable for leaving students with unmanageable debt.
body: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) blasted the Trump administration , saying the Department of Education’s rule limiting student loan programs targets women-dominated fields.

“I want to be very clear that what the Trump administration is doing, specifically, is attacking women’s ability to get an education,” Ocasio-Cortez said Thursday during the “It Shouldn’t Be This Hard” town hall in Escanaba, Michigan, with Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul el Sayed .

Under the DOE’s new rule, Student Tuition and Transparency System and Earnings Accountability , announced in June, undergraduate programs will need to show proof that their graduates earn more money than those without a college degree, and graduate programs need to show that their graduates earn more money than an individual with a bachelor’s degree. If they fail to show enough return on investment, they will be disqualified from federal student loan programs.
News about the rule recirculated in September with a Los Angeles Times article, suggesting fields like social work and mental health programs were at risk.
According to the Los Angeles Times , the DOE will prevent federal student loan access for college programs that don’t earn enough postgraduation.

“Because they put down that list on what they’re making harder, what they’re not going to give people student loans for, and it’s nurses, it’s teachers, it’s social workers,” Ocasio-Cortez said. “They don’t want women to go to college.”

Social work, education, and nursing are among “occupations with the largest share of women workers,” ranging from 83% to 97.4% in 2024, according to the Department of Labor. Ocasio-Cortez said when people “make a business” out of education, communities get left behind.
“I’m from the Bronx, where we desperately need doctors and have some of the highest maternal mortality rates in the United States,” Ocasio-Cortez said.
The DOE responded on X to an article by the New Republic in September, which cited the Los Angeles Times’s report, calling it “fake news.”

“This is fake news at its finest,” the DOE said. “First off, we’re not ‘banning’ any program. The federal government doesn’t set curriculum or programs. Here’s the truth: we are holding colleges accountable for leaving students worse off than if they never enrolled. Too many graduates report delaying major life milestones like buying a home or starting a family. Why? Because low return-on-investment programs saddled them with unmanageable debt that was never going to translate into a real-world job. Federal student loans are not a welfare program for failing college programs. American students deserve education and training pathways that prepare them for the workforce — and transparency about programs that will never pay off.”
SOCIAL MEDIA MELTS DOWN OVER MINOR TRUMP POLICY CHANGE ON STUDENT LOANS
The progressive Democrat said public universities should have free tuition and loans shouldn’t have interest, regardless of degrees.
“And beyond that, we have to really be asking ourselves, what is the utility of putting people in indentured servitude their entire lives for seeking an education?” Ocasio-Cortez said.

articles.headline: The Live-Action Street Fighter Movie Curse Has Yet To Be Broken
keyFacts: The new live-action Street Fighter movie is hindered by an identity crisis, inconsistent humor, and poor tonal direction.
Reviewers noted that while actors Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji deliver strong performances as Ken and Ryu, other characters like Chun-Li and Dan Hibiki fall flat.
Despite its writing and casting flaws, critics highlighted the film's consistent fight choreography and animated sequences as standout positive elements.
body: Street Fighter has long been more than just a fighting game. It’s impossible to discuss the most popular video game characters of all time without mentioning Chun-Li, Ryu, or Ken. For many of us, it shaped our '90s childhood at the arcade and served as our introduction to the fighting-game genre. It also has inspired multiple movies, comic books, an anime series and manga, on top of endless collaborations with other fighting game and comic book franchises.

Street Fighter's massive popularity is also a curse when it comes to live-action video game adaptations: 1994's Street Fighter and 2009's Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li were poorly received, despite both films having big budgets and being hyped among fans. The franchise failing twice as live-action films was an embarrassment to Capcom, so it's no surprise fans would be concerned about a third attempt at creating a decent live-action film.

When Kitao Sakurai was announced as the Street Fighter director, fans were both excited and concerned about him taking reins due to a history of working closely with Eric Andre. There was hope though, especially with the positive reception of a few other video game adaptations in the last few years: Perhaps the experience of Andre’s eccentric style of comedy could mean a more unconventional approach, similar to Zach Cregger’s approach with Resident Evil? Maybe the casting mix of Andre, pro wrestlers, martial artists, and, for some reason, podcaster Andrew Schulz could produce a very chaotic live-action comedy? Unfortunately, the questions around the movie's identity are ultimately what hurt the adaptation the most because, even with cartoonish action and plenty of attempts at humor, this Street Fighter movie doesn't really figure out what it is.

As with many other adaptations of Street Fighter, Ken is rich and famous, but he is also a shell of the fighter he once was--Ryu's absence has clearly taken its toll. Noah Centineo encapsulates Ken’s flashy personality and inflated ego excellently, while showcasing his more fragile and sensitive side as he reminisces about his past life with Ryu. Meanwhile, Ryu is now living in the shadows as a homeless ramen chef. Andrew Koji as Ryu is also fantastic casting: His serious and noble demeanor, even when it comes to making terrible ramen, feels natural. The first act of Street Fighter is engaging thanks to its focus on Ken and Ryu’s relationship. Their individual personality quirks should have set the tone for the rest of the film, but sadly it starts to have an identity crisis when it transitions to the main plot.

Don’t get me wrong--there are still many aspects of the film that capture the essence of the Street Fighter games: vibrant and thrilling fight scenes, cheesy dialogue, and some initially questionable casting choices that finally make sense after seeing the movie, especially Noah Centineo's Ken Masters. Street Fighter also immediately captivates you. Shortly after the Capcom logo hypes up the audience, the film transitions to a beautifully animated sequence that highlights the deep bond between Ryu and Ken. The animated sequences are the best Street Fighter has ever looked on screen, and luckily these scenes become a staple throughout the film to highlight the history between the two young fighters.

Once the opening credits are over, the film continues to learn into '90s nostalgia with cool environments and oddly endearing comedic moments, as it depicts Ken living his life in 1993 without Ryu, his childhood rival and sworn brother who has been missing for years. Ken and Ryu’s last moment together was witnessing the death of their master, Gouken, by the deity Akuma, who was awakened by Ryu’s powers in the first World Warrior Tournament. Haunted by the death of their mentor and blaming himself for causing it, Ryu has disappeared from the fighting world.

As with other movies based on fighting games, Street Fighter is in a rush to reach its core goal: Get Ryu and all the iconic characters to battle in the World Warrior Tournament. The rush never fully allows the audience to absorb the other characters and environment. This flaw could have been balanced with the proper tone and character focus, but Street Fighter fails to do so, doing the cast a disservice.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U6sbm1OaJb8&t=1s

The biggest letdown is the dialogue, as the humor is inconsistent and the movie never fully understands its own tone. Some characters, like Chun-Li and Dan Hibiki, don't fully commit to their personalities, either. Perhaps it’s the juvenile scripting or a casting issue, but either way, it felt like I was watching amateur actors in poor cosplay rather than seeing well-realized versions of these characters coming to life on screen. At first, the cringeworthy interactions got a few laughs out of me and had some very minor endearing moments, but it tries too hard to keep that comedic momentum going and fails miserably. The film forces you to accept bad writing and performances to drive it forward instead of allowing any of the interactions to feel natural.

Chun-Li’s character was the most disappointing to me. Her tragic backstory of avenging her father is already canon, which should’ve made it easier to adapt into a decent side plot with the right amount of tweaking, but instead she is incredibly flat and never fully fleshed out. Actor Callina Liang seems bored and uncomfortable throughout the entire film, even during her intense interactions with M. Bison and minor action moments. The writing and odd directional choices cater to the male gaze, making it obvious she was lazily written by a man. As one of the most capable and badass female characters in gaming, Chun-Li and, by extension, Callina Liang deserved better, and so did the fans.

The dumbfounding casting and scripting choice for this film was Andrew Schulz as Dan Hibiki. When Street Fighter was first announced, there was an immense amount of backlash for the casting of Andrew Schulz--a controversial podcaster and stand-up comedian. I could go on about the drama surrounding Schulz’s audience, his racism, hot takes, comedic style, etc., but for the sake of our collective sanity, I'll just say his inability to portray Dan’s character with any competency is yet another reason to question why he has any involvement in the production.

In Street Fighter canon, Dan is often portrayed as cocky and arrogant, while also being a bit inept as a fighter, yet in the movie his characterization is unclear--is he slimy or charismatic? Is he supposed to crack jokes, or just be an awkward friend? It’s also very odd how prevalent Dan is throughout the film, especially since he is without an arc or story to justify his frequent presence. The movie tries to sell you on a bond between Dan and Ken, but it’s a very uncomfortable friendship that never seems realistic or entertaining. The one vulnerable moment between them is immediately ruined by a weirdly homophobic joke--which, sadly, the film has a few of--and it comes off unsettlingly. In general, Dan and his casting are flat and uninspiring.

The initial joy of '90s nostalgia also wears off pretty quickly. It was certainly a welcome choice to have '90s hits like Montell Jordan’s “This is How We Do It” and 4 Non Blondes’ "What's Up?” feature on the soundtrack, but the movie goes on to then disregard the era the movie takes place in by blasting “Who Let the Dogs Out?,” a song that came out in 2000. While the film still remains pretty colorful, the lack of commitment to being period accurate undermines the vibe frequently.

The only aspect of Street Fighter that maintains a consistent quality is the fight choreography. This film is not afraid to embrace the cartoony vibes and reference unique movesets: hurricane kicks left and right, the iconic Hadoken, Blanka’s Electric Thunders, Zangief’s spinning piledriver, and a few more are sprinkled throughout each fight. Although the action was a little more limited due to the PG-13 rating, I was still impressed with the over-the-top stunts and tonally varied fights--silly spats with gags, a John Wick-style club brawl, and a few unique 1v1 battles that closely resemble what you would see in a Street Fighter game.

It’s also disappointing that a movie called Street Fighter fails to use its tournament structure for more individual fights between side characters. I would’ve loved to see Guile bust out some Sonic moves, or M. Bison doing anything other than complaining he needs more psycho power, but the film attempts to make up for it with a mix of impressive martial arts and campy action sequences elsewhere. Despite a PG-13 rating that limits the level of violence, the choreography team does fantastic work nevertheless. I just wish it had more Street Fighter style fights with different characters instead of being overshadowed by the goofy brawls you see in typical martial arts films.

Street Fighter is full of goofy action, colorful shots, and gorgeous animated sequences that focus on the bond between Ryu and Ken. It’s entertaining for some silly, mindless fun, but also a very messy movie that never quite figures out its tone and fails to sell you on its plot or characters. This is the best Street Fighter live action we have as far though, but unfortunately that's not an accolade worth bragging about.

articles.headline: English-born striker playing in ninth tier earns international call-up under ex-World Cup captain
keyFacts: Eighteen-year-old English ninth-tier striker Mohammed Mahe Khan has earned a call-up to the senior Bangladesh squad.
Bangladesh coach Thomas Dooley selected Khan for November's South Asian Championships without seeing him in a training camp.
Bangladesh will host the South Asian Championship starting on Thursday, November 5.
body: Mohammed Mahe Khan has earned a call-up to the senior Bangladesh squad for November’s South Asian Championships.
That is despite the fact that he is just 18 and is playing in the ninth tier of English football.
Dooley took charge of Bangladesh in May and won his debut match against San Marino Getty
The striker currently plays for Moulton in the South Premier Division, and he has been in great form.
Khan has nine goals in just seven games so far this season to earn his call-up.
And the man who has called him up is an American who captained the USMNT at the 1998 World Cup .
81-cap US international Thomas Dooley was born in Germany due to his father serving in the United States Army.
As a result, he spent the majority of his career in Germany in the Bundesliga .
And he is taking a big gamble on Khan, with the squad having to be selected before any training camp can take place.
He said: “We are going to take a young player, Mahe Khan. We will have a look at him in camp.
“However, we have to announce the final 28-man squad before the camp begins, so we won’t have the opportunity to assess him during training before making the decision.
“Selecting him now is almost like leaving it to chance.
“We believe he might be able to do the job we need. That’s the situation at the moment.”

South Asian Championship 2026
The South Asian Championship is the primary competition for countries that are part of the South Asian Football Federation.
Bangladesh are the hosts this year, with the tournament kicking off on Thursday, November 5 and coming to an end on Tuesday, November 17.
It is contested between six sides, with every game being played at the national stadium in Dhaka.
This will be the 15th edition of the tournament, with India being the most successful team.
They have won it nine times and are the highest-ranked team on the FIFA list.
Bangladesh won it once in 2003 and will be looking to claim it once more on home soil.

Dooley’s career
Dooley played the majority of his games for Kaiserslautern and won the Bundesliga with them and Homburg, but his form did get him a move to a couple of Germany’s biggest clubs.

articles.headline: Trump’s plan to deport a member of Congress
keyFacts: Ilhan Omar (D-MN) during a news conference at the US Capitol on February 24, 2026.

Welcome to The Logoff: Donald Trump wants to deport a member of Congress.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) during a news conference at the US Capitol on February 24, 2026. | Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: Donald Trump wants to deport a member of Congress.

What’s happening? On Monday, Homeland Security officers raided the Washington, DC, home of US Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) in an investigation reportedly tied to immigration paperwork filled out by her father when she was a minor.

That was, at the time, more than enough cause for alarm. Trump’s animosity toward Omar , who is Somali-American and an outspoken critic of the administration, is well-known, and the raid is an extraordinary violation of the Justice Department’s usual rule to avoid taking visible action around politically sensitive cases within 60 days of an election.

On Wednesday evening, however, we learned more about the raid from the Wall Street Journal . The Omar investigation, the Journal reported, is explicitly aimed at stripping Omar of her citizenship — and thus her ability to hold office — and deporting her.

How would they do that? Omar came to the US as a refugee when she was 12 and became a US citizen when she was 17. The Trump administration’s investigation is said to focus on whether she or her family misrecorded her age in order to more easily gain citizenship.
The government cannot unilaterally denaturalize a citizen, however; it would have to ask a court to do so.

What’s the context? Historically, it’s rare for the US to strip citizenship from naturalized US citizens. But doing so at volume has been a major, if less visible, priority for the second Trump administration.

As of earlier this year, NBC News reported , DOJ was targeting hundreds of people for possible denaturalization, and has reportedly hoped to put forward hundreds of new cases per month (though successfully stripping them of citizenship is another matter).
Why does this matter? Trump’s campaign to bend the traditionally nonpartisan DOJ into a tool to punish and harass his enemies has been one of the major stories of his second term.

Even if it never advances beyond Monday’s raid, an investigation targeting Omar’s citizenship with the eventual goal of deporting her from the US represents a new and even more dangerous evolution of that effort — and it threatens to move the US to a far darker place, where citizenship and the rights it guarantees are predicated on the president’s goodwill.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

body: A pro Dota 2 player is claiming that he had to play a full Dota match in front of police officers to prove his identity.

According to Nuengnara "23savage" Teeramahanon, who currently plays hard carry for Xipto eSports, the team’s boot camp in Kuala Lumpur was raided by police Sunday evening. In a post made on Facebook Monday night, 23savage describes the police placing the team in handcuffs and confiscating their belongings.

The officers proceeded to interrogate the players about why they were in the city and whether they were really pro players. According to 23savage, one of the officers was familiar with Dota, and was willing to scroll the player’s Instagram for proof of his pro career.

DotA2

A photo 23savage had recently posted of himself and popular Malaysian influencer Ms. Puiyi was, according to the post, somewhat acceptable evidence. Enough evidence, in fact, for the police officers to remove his handcuffs and test what really mattered: how good he is at defending the ancients.

23savage proceeded to start up a Dota match right in front of the police officers, dropping 23 kills as the hard carry Kez. The Dota player alleges that this was enough proof to convince the officers to let the team go, and also that they stole two jars of Nutella on their way out.

Commenters on the post quickly doubted 23savage’s claims, presuming the post to be a joke, but 23savage has been actively defending his story in the replies. Reddit users continue to doubt the hard carry player, while others jokingly claim 23savage’s story is saving Valve’s MOBA.

The incident doesn’t seem to have had much impact on Xipto, who have been climbing the ranks of SEA Dota. articles.headline: Welp, all of you RuneScape folks who hate Reignited have gotten your wish, as the controversial MMO rejig has been cancelled
keyFacts: Jagex cancelled RuneScape Reignited, a controversial new character type and economy, following negative feedback from players.
Jagex stated they cancelled the project to avoid repeating past mistakes and to protect the existing community.
Jagex will instead release the Adventure Guide and the first part of the Remastered Journey on December 2nd.
body: Welp, that was short lived. Earlier this month, Jagex made some big RuneScape announcements, namely that they're making a fourth version of the MMO (aptly, currently called RuneScape 4), but also the arrival of RuneScape Reignited, a new character type that would come with its own, new economy. The intention here seemingly was to bring new people in to breathe some life back into the game. This did not go down well with the old timers. And now, it's been flat out cancelled.

"First of all, thank you for all the feedback since the announcement at Runefest," a blog post from Jagex explained. "We received a ton of different perspectives from all of you, and we truly appreciate everyone sharing their views. It is super important to us because the last time we didn't listen to player feedback, combat changed forever. And it has taken us over a decade to recover from that. Now I said on stage that we would not repeat the same mistakes of the past, and I truly stand by that. Considering this, we have made the decision to cancel Reignited."

Jagex go on to note that it was clearly they "missed the mark on this, and so we are not moving forward with it. Our goal is to see Runescape grow again, with returning players coming back and new players joining, but never at the expense of our existing community." That kind of leaves that original December 2nd launch date in an awkward spot, so to make up for that, the developer will be "releasing the Adventure Guide and the first part of the Remastered Journey, alongside a host of other improvements, some of which you've all been talking about over the last week."

A 10 day free trial is still running between December 2nd and 12th, with any new characters, or any that haven't been in active membership since June 2nd, "will be able to freely access RuneScape Members worlds and content during the 10 day period." So, if you were someone considering jumping into the game thanks to Reignited, it sounds like this is an in at the very least. Quite the mess Jagex have got themselves in here! Hope they can all weather the storm.

articles.headline: Donor slaps suit against Guilfoyle, threatens to release dirt on Trump if fraudster isn’t extradited: ‘This is not extortion’
keyFacts: Lawyer Eric Deters filed a defamation lawsuit against former US Ambassador Kimberley Guilfoyle over text messages she allegedly claimed were generated by artificial intelligence.
Deters stated he will drop the lawsuit if President Trump secures the extradition of alleged fraudster Abubakar Atiq Durrani from Pakistan.
Guilfoyle's lawyer told The Post that the lawsuit is frivolous and that their response will speak for itself.
body: WASHINGTON — A lawyer and former Trump donor unveiled a defamation lawsuit against former US Ambassador to Greece Kimberley Guilfoyle as part of an apparent ploy to win the extradition of an alleged fraudster.

Eric Deters, who exposed text messages Guilfoyle sent begging him to pay off some $100,000 in her personal debts last year, announced the suit after the former Fox News personality allegedly claimed the texts were generated by artificial intelligence.

Deters explained that he will drop the suit if President Trump gets alleged fraudster physician Abubakar Atiq Durrani extradited from his suspected whereabouts in Pakistan and probes the judiciary’s handling of that case.

“This is not extortion,” Deters declared in a video post on social media. “Nothing I am asking for or doing is unlawful. I am playing hardball because the doctor Durrani victims deserve hardball on their behalf.”

Guilfoyle made a vague public claim that the accusations against her are “false,” but privately told White House officials that the bombshell texts begging Deters for money were AI-generated, the Wall Street Journal reported. The texts — and the distraction Guilfoyle created for the White House — prompted Trump to ask for her resignation.
Deters, who has been on a crusade to get Durrani extradited on behalf of the doctor’s victims, teased that he has more dirt on other Trump world figures as well.

“Information is pouring into me. And I got off the phone today from someone in Greece,” he added. “By the end of tomorrow I am going to play for you a phone recording that is the most explosive, most devastating information about Kimberly Guilfoyle to date.”
“No one in the media has it,” he added. “And I am going to play for you a 16-minute phone conversation.”

Deters, who said he is representing himself in the defamation suit as it plays out in court, also teased plans to pursue depositions of Donald Trump Jr. and Guilfoyle. The two got engaged in 2020, but officially cut it off in 2024.
The White House revealed Tuesday that Guilfoyle was asked to step down, and she announced her resignation shortly thereafter.
“This might just bring down the entire Trump administration, an administration which I have supported from day one, whose policies I still support,” Deters boldly declared.
“It also may end the JD Vance, Marco Rubio ticket after you hear the phone call that I’m going to play tomorrow.”

Durrani had been indicted in 2013 on numerous charges for allegedly getting close to 600 people to undergo unnecessary, risky spinal surgical operations. But he is believed to have fled the country before he could face trial.
Deters did legal work for numerous victims who suffered from Durrani’s alleged push for them to undergo unnecessary medical procedures.
He is also demanding that he receive an admission that he “did not blackmail” Guilfoyle and that he does not owe her money.
“The lawsuit is clearly frivolous on its face. Our upcoming response will speak for itself,” Guilfoyle’s lawyer told The Post.

articles.headline: The UK may expand the BBC license fee, charging residents to watch streaming services
keyFacts: UK leaders will propose extending the BBC license fee to cover video streaming platforms later this year.
Proponents argue the change will prevent people from avoiding the tax by watching content on computers or mobile devices.
The additional funding would reportedly support local journalism, combat misinformation, and address BBC budget issues.
body: The UK may expand the BBC license fee, charging residents to watch streaming services
If the proposal is enacted, it could cost $240 a year to watch YouTube in the UK.

The UK government will consider charging residents a national fee to access video streaming content, meaning it may cost almost $240 a year just to watch YouTube in the region. The Independent reported that later this year, UK leaders will propose extending the BBC license fee to cover streaming video platforms.

For our non-UK readers, the license fee is responsible for a large amount of funding for the BBC. It is levied on all residents who watch content on a television, whether or not that content includes BBC programming. The standard fee is currently £180 (~$239) a year. Paying the fee grants viewers access to all domestic TV channels, several pay TV services, live TV shown via streaming platforms and on-demand content via BBC iPlayer.

The proposed changes would expand the license fee and apply it to several streaming services such as Netflix, Amazon, Disney+ and YouTube. Proponents of the change argue that people can use those platforms on their mobile devices or computers rather than their TVs to evade the tax. "It's not fair that people are essentially able to watch television content but avoid the license fee," an unnamed source told The Independent about the proposed changes.

The additional funding from expanding the license fee would reportedly be put toward supporting local journalism and combatting misinformation campaigns. The UK's national broadcaster is also facing budget issues, with a 2 million decline in the number of license fees paid over the past five years, according to The Independent. Despite that decrease, YouGov data suggests the BBC remains the most popular media platform in the UK.

The BBC recently announced that it would begin streaming a 24/7 news channel on YouTube for viewers in the UK and the US. The broadcaster already has similar channels active in Australia, Kenya, Nigeria and Poland.

articles.headline: Plex now helps sell movie theater tickets
keyFacts: Plex partnered with Fandango to allow US users to buy movie theater tickets directly from movie title pages.
The integration lets Fandango leverage Plex streaming data to gain insight into audience intent and drive ticket sales.
The partnership also provides studios and advertisers with direct attribution to measure how campaigns translate into ticket purchases.
body: Plex, which made a name for itself by letting users share movies they own, is now helping sell movie theater tickets. The company is looking to monetize its content-discovery capabilities and expand its business beyond its media server software.
Plex partnered with Fandango, which has sold movie tickets since 2000, to drive ticket sales from people searching for movies to stream. Per the announcement:

Starting today, Plex users in the US will see a Fandango ticketing option on title pages for movies currently playing in theaters, allowing them to click through to Fandango to find showtimes and purchase tickets. The integration also enables direct attribution through Kochava, giving studios and advertisers greater visibility into how campaigns and audience engagement translate into ticket sales.

Fandango says it sells tickets for 31,000 movie theater screens in the US. The Plex deal allows it to leverage data from Plex’s streaming service (Plex claims users of the service “make more than 100 million streaming decisions each month”), including “ratings and cross-platform viewing” to gain “insight into audience intent,” the announcement said.

“Plex has a unique view into what movie fans are actively considering, from what they’re searching for to what they’re watching across services,” Jerramy Hainline, executive vice president at Fandango, said in a statement. “By connecting those discovery signals with Fandango ticketing, we’re making it easier for fans to turn that interest into a trip to the theater, while giving studios and advertisers a more direct, measurable path to ticket sales.”

keyFacts: Universal Pictures announced that the next movie in the franchise is titled The Mummy: Book of the Dead and will be released on Oct. 15, 2027.

The film's subtitle and returning characters strongly imply that the villain Imhotep may be featured, though official plot details have not been released.
body: Mark your calendars, because the 27-year-old The Mummy franchise officially returns exactly one year from today. To mark the occasion, Universal Pictures finally revealed the title for the next The Mummy movie.
Now called The Mummy: Book of the Dead, the sequel will hit theaters Oct. 15, 2027

The Mummy: Book of the Dead will reunite Rachel Weisz's Evie Carnahan and Brendan Fraser's Rick O'Connell after Weisz (wisely) sat out the third film and Evie was recast with Maria Bello taking on the role. Recent set photos of a very stylish Weisz have indicated that Book of the Dead might take place in the late 1950s. Other photos have shown Fraser's new look as O'Connell. But, now that the official title has been revealed, there's still one major question we're wondering.
Will The Mummy: Book of the Dead rehash Imhotep's story again?

The first two The Mummy movies center around titular mummy Imhotep and his attempts at coming back to life. He's resurrected via the Book of the Dead, so the subtitle for the next movie highly implies he'll be a key figure in The Mummy: Book of the Dead.

Add in the fact that Oded Fehr is returning as Ardeth Bay, and it seems all but certain Imhotep will play a role, though official plot details for the next movie have yet to be shared. Ardeth Bay leads the Medjai, a group of warriors whose whole deal is to make sure Imhotep stays dead. Presumably, if Bay is around, then someone might be trying to bring Imhotep back to life (hey, third time's the charm), like, say Beni... who seemingly died in the first movie. Kevin J. O'Connor is reprising his role as Beni for Book of the Dead, so maybe Beni's not dead after all, and instead doing Imhotep's bidding again.

Imhotep's actor Arnold Vosloo hasn't officially been confirmed to reprise his role, but earlier this year John Hannah (Jonathan Carnahan) said Vosloo would be back. We'll learn more the closer we get to The Mummy: Book of the Dead's release and as trailers get released for it. Until then, time to watch 1999's The Mummy for the 100th time.

articles.headline: Less than 2 weeks after announcing RuneScape Reignited, Jagex is scrapping the whole thing
keyFacts: Developer Jagex cancelled RuneScape Reignited less than two weeks after its initial announcement following heavy player backlash over community splits and subscription fees.
Mod Ryan stated in a blog post that the studio missed the mark and decided not to move forward with the project.
Jagex will offer a ten-day free trial for new and returning players starting on December 2.
body: Life comes at you fast, as the saying goes, and the folks at RuneScape developer Jagex can sure attest to that. Less than two weeks after announcing RuneScape Reignited—essentially a way for new and lapsed players to restart their adventures from fresh on separate, unique servers—the studio has decided to cancel it.

There was trouble with RuneScape Reignited almost right from the start, with complaints ranging from a potential community split to restrictions on character interactions and the need to pay for a separate subscription. Just a few days after the initial announcement, Jagex apologized for making veteran players feel like they were being shunted aside, and said it was "exploring a heavy set of revisions to Reignited based on your feedback."

A few days after that, it laid out a more specific list of intended alterations, and invited more feedback from players, "so we can follow up next week with more of our thoughts." With that feedback now received, it seems that Jagex has heard enough.

"It is clear that we missed the mark on this, and so we are not moving forward with it," Mod Ryan—associate creative director Ryan Philpott—said in a blog post announcing the cancellation. "Our goal is to see Runescape grow again, with returning players coming back and new players joining, but never at the expense of our existing community."

It's a very sudden about-face, but not unprecedented. In 2023, for instance, Jagex dropped a new RuneScape battle pass in the wake of massive player backlash; in 2025, the studio scrapped "Treasure Hunter" microtransactions, in what Jagex CEO Jon Bellamy said was "part of a wider transformation across Jagex, which is seeing a renewed commitment to delivering deeper value, greater fairness and long-term improvements for players."

It hasn't been entirely smooth sailing: Recent price hikes have not gone over well (no surprise there, though), and Jagex's cowardly decision to scrap in-game Pride Month events was allowed to stand despite players absolutely mauling the studio for it. But in terms of gameplay, at least, Jagex has demonstrated a willingness to react with relative haste when it's blown things sufficiently badly—and this definitely qualifies.

Despite the cancellation, Philpott invited new and returning players to jump into the game with a 10 day free trial beginning on December 2, which will offer full access to all worlds and content. The 2027 roadmap for RuneScape also remains in place:

"The future of RuneScape is still extremely bright," Philpott concluded. "RuneScape will always be built for and defined by its community. So please keep letting us know when you feel we're getting it wrong and shout with that same energy when you think we're getting it right too."
