articles.headline: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay on the importance of failure and bouncing back from it
keyFacts: Amazon executive Panos Panay stated at TechCrunch Disrupt that failure is a necessary part of building a successful product.
Panay cited his experience with Microsoft's Surface RT tablet, which resulted in a nearly $1 billion write-down, as a major personal failure.
Panay advised startup founders to accept failure without making excuses, learn from past mistakes, and stay committed to their vision.
body: Amazon executive Panos Panay has a message for startup founders: Failure is an inevitable, required part of building a successful product.

Panay, Amazon SVP of Devices, Alexa, and Leo, shared that advice onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco, drawing on his own experience at Microsoft, where he spent more than 19 years and weathered one particularly expensive failure.

“You have to be willing to fail, and actually, not just willing, you actually have to go fail,” Panay said. “If you haven’t failed, you probably haven’t pushed the boundary. It’s literally about harvesting the lessons learned when you fail. You have to be willing to face it, and as you face it, learn from it.”

Panay said it’s possible to recover from all sorts of failures, even catastrophic ones, noting that he experienced one himself at Microsoft. He described the launch of the Surface RT, Microsoft’s first tablet computer, as a significant failure during his tenure at the company, one that ultimately led to a nearly $1 billion write-down.

“I remember being on the front cover of a newspaper, and it just said failure,” Panay said. “But, here’s the thing, it was easy to admit failure. The trick was, and always is, did you harvest the learnings and understand what happened? All right. What did you learn? Because the failure wasn’t that moment. It was decisions that led up to it two years before that, whether the software wasn’t complete or the inventory was wrong or how we balanced into retail. There were all these steps along the way.”
He said founders need to be willing to understand what went wrong, and avoid making excuses, and ultimately accept the failure.

“Here’s the other side of it,” he said. “You want to succeed, yeah? You take that failure, but you don’t let go of your vision. That’s it. Surface has done pretty well. You don’t let go of your vision. You don’t break it.”

Panay emphasized the importance of staying committed to a vision, learning from experience, and moving quickly. He believes that by embracing failure and learning from setbacks, founders can adapt and make progress faster, even as they encounter new obstacles.

“It goes back to the same fundamental, like, have you learned?” he said. “Were you learning along the way? Because if you were learning, then you just change your vector. Usually, it’s not 180 degrees. Usually, it’s just 30 degrees. Take your lessons learned, change a little bit, adapt your vision where it needs to be, and then go. I believe there’s people that hang on too long, but it’s because they haven’t accepted the moment of failure at all.”

articles.headline: Give him a hand: Dev publishes 25-year-old Palm OS tools to GitHub
keyFacts: Swedish developer Aaron Ardiri published about a gigabyte of Palm OS development resources on GitHub to preserve them for retro computing enthusiasts.
Ardiri stated the files had been in his personal backups for over 25 years after his time developing Palm OS applications.
Ardiri excluded materials like ROM images and commercial apps to avoid copyright issues during this historical preservation effort.
body: A small but active community of retro computing enthusiasts is working to keep Palm OS alive, and a developer who recently became aware of their existence has just handed them a treasure trove of code he had no idea was still useful. Swedish developer Aaron Ardiri published around a gigabyte of Palm OS development resources on GitHub on Thursday in a bid to preserve them for community consumption. Prior to their upload, Ardiri told The Register that the files were languishing in his own personal backups for more than 25 years, preserved only for his own records as part of his past as a developer of Palm OS applications. “Everything in the archive was accumulated during my years as an active Palm OS developer,” Ardiri explained in an email. “It includes SDKs, technical documentation, conference presentations, development utilities, examples, and some limited system source code that was originally made available to developers to help them understand the operating system's UI and internal components.” One gigabyte of such info might not seem like a lot today, but back in the halcyon era of the PalmPilot, that was a whole heap of valuable data. Ardiri had previously published source code from his own Palm OS apps on GitHub for those who were interested in it, but he had assumed it was just for public record and that no one would really want to muck about with old Palm OS apps. “A developer recently submitted a pull request to my original Lemmings source repository, adding HiRes+ display support for the Palm Tungsten T3,” Ardiri explained. “I had no idea people were still actively developing and improving this software more than two decades later.” That sent him down a rabbit hole. He soon realized there were Palm OS enthusiasts on Reddit, Discord, and other online communities all looking for resources to keep their vintage hardware alive and their retro software viable. “It made me realize that the old development resources sitting on my backup drives might actually be useful to people today,” he said. And now here we are, with a nice, fat GitHub repo full of resources Palm OS users can make use of. It’s worth noting that just because Ardiri has published this stuff on GitHub, that doesn’t mean it’s open source and ripe for the picking. He’s taken steps to avoid stepping on any copyright toes by leaving out things like Palm OS ROM images, firmware, simulators, and commercial apps that he felt he ought not to distribute as he didn’t have explicit permission. Ardiri sees this as a historical preservation effort, not an attempt to circumvent IP laws. “A lot of early mobile development knowledge has disappeared with old websites, developer forums, and documentation archives. Some of it survives only in personal collections like mine,” Ardiri told us. He said that he’s thrilled to have been introduced to the world of Palm enthusiasts, and recently passed off more than 50 old Palm OS devices to Russian dev and Palm OS preservationist Dmitry Grinberg. “This has been an unexpected rediscovery of a period of my career that I thought was largely behind me,” Ardiri told us. “It's clear that Palm OS has a much more active community than I realized … the repository is my contribution to those efforts, providing a historical record of what development looked like when Palm OS was a thriving commercial platform.” It makes you wonder what other digital gold is sitting in backups just waiting to be discovered. Take this as a sign to take a look through your old drives – you never know what you might find that someone has long been looking for. ®

articles.headline: Ilhan Omar's husband snaps over rumors she fled US after federal immigration fraud raid
keyFacts: Federal agents raided the Washington, D.C., home of Representative Ilhan Omar as part of a criminal immigration fraud investigation, according to reports.
Tim Mynett stated to Fox News Digital that he has no concerns regarding the federal investigation into his wife's immigration pathway.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced that her office is investigating Omar's financial disclosures after her office amended a filing about her net worth.
body: While Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., has not been seen publicly since federal agents raided her Washington, D.C., residence on Monday, her political consultant husband was once again spotted emerging from their shared rental home this week.

Tim Mynett was seen Wednesday stepping out in the neighborhood to walk their Golden Labrador Retriever dog Teddy, a second time later that same day to take out the trash and a third time to walk out his wife's staffer.
"There are rumors that the congresswoman left the country, is that true?" Mynett was asked while on an evening walk with Teddy.

"You guys are annoying the hell out of all the neighbors around here, man," he told Fox News Digital when approached about the developments this week, including President Donald Trump weighing in on the saga.

One of Omar's congressional staffers was captured the same day bringing into the couple's home two large bags from fast food chain Burger King. Security escorted her to the door and staked out in front of the house after she entered with the meal.
ILHAN OMAR’S EMBATTLED HUSBAND APPEARS AT SCENE OF HSI RAID IN MIDST OF CRIMINAL FRAUD INVESTIGATION

Rumors swirled that Omar fled from the country following the raid carried out by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) as part of a criminal fraud investigation looking into the Somali-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork, as first reported by Fox News Digital.
Omar’s cellphone and passport were reportedly seized by federal authorities during the search.

The congresswoman's staff helped to get her birth year adjusted from 1981 to 1982 in the Minnesota Legislative Reference Library, according to reporters. Omar gained citizenship automatically through her father’s naturalization since she was reportedly 17 years old at the time. If Omar was born in 1981, she would have been 18 years old, meaning the validity of her citizenship could be threatened because she was no longer a minor.
The altered birthdate was published during her entire time serving in Minnesota’s House and for months into her time serving in Congress.

When asked about the federal investigation earlier this week, Mynett told Fox News Digital he has "no concerns" about what federal authorities will find on his wife while investigating her immigration pathway.
"My wife came here when she was 12 years old as a child war refugee," Mynett said. "No concerns."

His comments to Fox News Digital come after Omar’s relatives were reportedly issued subpoenas as part of HSI’s investigation into the congresswoman's immigration paperwork. At least two of Omar's relatives were subpoenaed, one of which is reportedly Omar’s sister, Sahra Noor.
ILHAN OMAR’S HUSBAND INSISTS HE HAS ‘NO CONCERNS’ AMID FEDERAL IMMIGRATION INVESTIGATION

Fox News Digital asked Mynett about President Donald Trump publicly questioning Omar’s net worth by alleging on Truth Social that her accountant may have reported fraudulent money when her previous financial disclosure listed the couple's shared net worth as high as $30 million.

"Why did Ilhan Omar report a Net Worth of up to 30 Million Dollars just a short time ago, and then immediately say, "Oh, I made a mistake! It’s really $100,000." Could it be that her highly paid accountant actually reported the money that was stolen from her fraudulent activities in Minnesota? Would something like that be possible? Do you think the accountant actually gave the right number the first time, 30 Million Dollars, and then she was forced to disavow because she never would have been able to report where that much money came from? She must have freaked out when she saw that money!" Trump posted to Truth Social on Tuesday.

"Where did her house come from, where did her cars come from, and what about her lovely place in Washington, D.C.? I didn’t know that Congressmen and women made that kind of money, but I do know her husband, according to information and belief, makes almost nothing, so it couldn’t have come from him. How many people did she illegally bring into our Country from Somalia? America wants answers, and we want them, NOW!"
Mynett is at the center of yet another investigation into Omar — this time looking into her finances.
Following Monday’s HSI raid, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro said Tuesday that her office is also investigating Omar's financial disclosures about reporting of her and Mynett’s shared net worth.
OMAR FACES MOUNTING SCRUTINY AFTER FRAUD RINGLEADER SENTENCED TO 41 YEARS

Scrutiny of Omar's finances intensified after her 2024 congressional financial disclosure listed business interests associated with Mynett valued between $6 million and $30 million. Omar's office subsequently said the figures were incorrect and amended the filing.

The largest change in the documents was from Mynett’s assets . His reported ownership interests in both his winery and venture capital advisory firm, which were previously valued in the millions of dollars, are listed with no value now.

In Omar’s 2024 financial disclosure records, Mynett’s share in his winery was valued between $1 million and $5 million, and his share at the venture capital advisory firm was valued between $5 million and $25 million. Now, his equity interests are both listed at $0.

Omar's office previously told Fox News Digital that Mynett has partners in both businesses and said the earlier disclosure mistakenly reflected the businesses' total equity rather than his ownership interest. The office also said the original filing listed assets without accounting for liabilities.
Officials noted that the investigation into Omar's financial disclosures is unrelated to the raid on her home.

GOAL! Brighton 2-0 Kauno Zalgiris (Hinshelwood, 45+2 mins)

Goalless after 40 minutes, Brighton go in at half-time two up after Jack Hinshelwood’s goal survives a VAR check to see if the ball went out of play in the build-up. They’ve had 10 shots so far, three on target; Kauno are yet to have an on-target shot of any kind.
What a header that is! The ball is crossed in from the right and met by Evanilson, on the near side of the near post, who somehow power-flicks it high, looping over the keeper and in at the far post!

8.43pm: “If Benfica’s Duran Duran tribute act keeps churning out the hits you can Save a Prayer for Celtic’s chances,” essays Peter Oh, whose earlier effort about Reflex saves was perhaps better but got lost in a barrage of goals, so is rewarded for persistence. Talking of which …

Celtic give the ball away on halfway, two quick passes send Duran running into the area, and he pushes the ball quite wide before benefiting from Viljami Sinisalo’s puzzling positioning and useless star-jump to turn the ball in with a low shot! This is looking pretty grim for Martin O’Neill’s side.
Hearts take the lead! A corner is swung into the area, hilariously miskicked by Mendy, headed goalwards, and then turned in from close range by Oisin McEntee!

8.32pm: “Evening Simon,” writes Simon McMahon. “Celtic are always capable of scoring, but I worry about them defensively. Well, I say worry, but I love it really, as do most fans of other Scottish clubs, who for years have seen the self styled ‘Bhoys’ buy their best players for a pittance, win everything domestically, and then blame ‘lack of competition’ for their European failure. The fact that they are still harking back to 1967, undoubtedly a significant achievement at the time, but also nearly 60 years ago, only confirms how far they have fallen.” You can’t really blame Celtic for the fact they find it a bit hard to win major European trophies these days, though, the whole world of football has shifted against them.
8.30pm: Bournemouth have the ball in the net after a bit of a post-corner scramble, but the referee harshly disallows it for some kind of push or other (actually, on reviewing, probably a handball).

Nice work down the left from Benfica, who play the ball around long enough for the entire Celtic defence to fall entirely asleep, whereupon the chip it into the box and onto the right foot of Alexander Bah, whose run has gone unnoticed by the snoozing Celtic backline, and he volleys it in!
8.21pm: And it’s Celta Vigo 1-0 Juventus, Hugo Alvarez eventually poking in after the ball was played from the right-hand side of the penalty area to the left.

8.20pm: And now they’re flying in! Atalanta double their lead through a penalty, Freiburg go a goal up against Jablonec through Vincenzo Grifo’s excellent free-kick, and Sint-Truiden actually do go 1-0 up against Iberia, their previous opening goal having been ruled out for offside.

8.15pm: More goals to report, as Sint-Truiden go 1-0 up against Iberia 1999 while Ararat take the lead at Jagiellonia Bialistyock, who are undone by a goal down the middle and Zidane Banjaqui pokes it through the advancing goalkeeper’s legs just before the two of them collide.

8.12pm: OFI take the lead against Rennes, who play themselves into trouble as they’re pressed hard. OFI nick the ball, cross it into the box and Taxiarchis Fountas is entirely unmarked as he heads it back across the keeper and in.

8.04pm: A ghastly start for Celtic, who have conceded a penalty with not even four minutes on the clock after Jhon Duran hits the deckbbc. And meanwhile Atalanta have taken the lead against Pafos in the Conference League, Eljif Elmas capping a nice move by sweeping the ball home from the edge of the area.
Pre-match reading: Here’s Jeff Rueter on Feyenoord’s Gjivai Zechiël, who is apparently quite good.

Nailing the pronunciation of Gjivai Zechiël may be a challenge for some, but it’ll be worth the effort. The Dutch G is a guttural one, not struck with a tongue so much as residing under one’s uvula like a congested H: kHEE-vye. The surname is a bit more straightforward: ZEH-kee-el, a natural decrescendo of emphasis with every syllable.
Used in a sentence: Gjivai Zechiël is one of the hottest midfielders in Europe, enjoying arguably the most rapid emergence of any high-level player in 2026.

The manager [Marco Silva] came here because he wanted to win things, and you’ve got a good chance when you’re at Benfica. We have to earn the right to play, do lots of things off the ball, but most importantly when you’re on it, have the confidence. We’ll have the opportunity to play, and that’s exactly what you want: confidence in yourself, and confidence in your teammates.

Team news is starting to land and I’m going to pour it all in here, starting with Benfica v Celtic and news that not only is Camilo Durán but Jhon Durán starts for Benfica, making this very much a Durán v Durán affair, and if that isn’t an excuse for enjoying some fine 80s music I don’t know what is.

articles.headline: US justice department sues California over alleged noncitizen voting
keyFacts: The US Department of Justice sued California to prevent the state from tabulating certain mail-in ballots in the midterm elections.
California election officials refused to process a federal list of 20,000 flagged voters, citing security and voter-purge concerns.
The lawsuit asks a federal court to require California to set aside and verify flagged ballots before counting them.
body: The US Department of Justice sued California on Thursday, seeking a court order to prevent the state from tabulating certain ballots cast in the midterm elections.

The suit came two days after the department made a specious demand to the state. On Tuesday, the department sent election officials in Los Angeles county a thumb drive with a handwritten password purporting to contain the names of noncitizens registered to vote. The department asked officials to confirm the citizenship of anyone on the list and set aside ballots from those whose status could not be confirmed. It gave the state 48 hours – an extremely narrow window – to take action. It did not provide details on how it came up with the names on the list. In its lawsuit, filed in federal court in the central district of California, the justice department said it had provided the state with more than 20,000 names of likely noncitizens.
The Los Angeles county clerk and recorder, Dean Logan, said his office would not review the list, in part because it didn’t consider the USB drive secure.

In a statement on Wednesday, the California secretary of state, Shirley Weber, a Democrat, said the justice department had not provided the list of voters to her office. “The [justice department’s] relentless efforts to unlawfully gain access to states’ protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections,” Weber said.
Justice department lawyers are asking the court to order the state not to count votes from those it had flagged.

“This Court should enjoin California from presently tabulating vote-by-mail ballots from likely noncitizens in the upcoming federal election until the voter’s citizenship status can be determined,” the lawsuit said. “This Court should order California (1) to set aside vote-by-mail ballots from persons identified by the Federal Government likely to be noncitizens and (2) to independently – or in collaboration with the Federal Government – verify their citizenship status (beyond relying on unverified statements of citizenship necessary to registering) before tabulating their vote-by-mail ballot.”

The request to block tabulation comes amid concerns that Donald Trump and his allies will interfere in the counting of votes in the midterm elections, in which Republicans are expected to lose seats in Congress.

The Trump administration’s methodology for identifying noncitizens has come under scrutiny. Earlier this year, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said there could be as many as 278,000 noncitizens on the rolls in four states, including more than 190,000 in California and about 16,000 in Nevada.

Officials at the DHS refused to share their methodology with Nevada election officials and later turned over just 185 names of people it had a strong belief were noncitizens. When Nevada officials investigated, they found every one of those people was a citizen.

Richard Hasen, an election law scholar at UCLA, described the justice department’s efforts in California as “a nice publicity stunt that gets attention for [the justice department] and reinforces the notion among the president’s most ardent supporters that California is not doing enough to combat voter fraud”.

“The Department of Justice has no standing to tell states and localities to go in and remove voters from voting rolls in the midst of an election. In fact, the National Voter Registration Act bars systematic purges of ineligible voters in the 90-day period before the election,” he wrote in a blogpost. “The purpose of this provision, unsurprisingly, is to stop false positives, that is the removal of eligible voters who are mistakenly flagged as noncitizens. A rushed process would almost certainly lead to disenfranchisement.”

articles.headline: Renting? These 2 new Apple smart home devices are worth your money (and these 5 are not)
keyFacts: Apple introduced the Apple Home Collection, including new smart home products ranging from $40 sensors to $400 security cameras.
ZDNet reported that specific plug-in devices like the LG Indoor Cam and LG Outdoor Cam work well for renters because they require no permanent installation.
Apple stated that its smart home devices use on-device AI, Private Cloud Compute, and end-to-end encryption to secure user data.
body: Apple recently introduced a handful of new smart home products, with its first smart panel, the HomeView; a new HomePod mini; an Apple TV 4K; and a complete Home Collection with nine smart home devices. Starting at $40 for smart sensors and up to $400 for security cameras, the Apple Home Collection is not exactly budget-friendly, but could it still be right for renters?

As a homeowner with a mix of smart home ecosystems (including Apple Home), I often wonder about the audience companies intend to target with these kinds of devices. I’ve been a renter myself, and I know how creative you have to be with your smart home setup, given landlord and lease restrictions.
More from ZDNET
Good for renters: LG’s Indoor Cam

The LG Indoor Cam is a pan/tilt security camera that looks quite different from comparable options, and has a unique privacy feature. Unlike most indoor cameras that require you to either manually activate privacy mode or set a schedule for it, the Apple Home app triggers it automatically when you come home. While Apple doesn’t specify exactly what triggers this action, it’s likely that it happens based on an iPhone’s location and proximity.

There’s no question that, at $200, the LG Indoor Cam is expensive. There are other indoor cameras with privacy features available, even if they go into privacy mode on a schedule, that are far more affordable and may offer better features, including the $60 Anker Eufy E220, the $140 Anker Eufy S350, and the $99 Aqara Camera Hub G3.
Also: The best iPhone Duo cases in 2026: Expert recommended

The camera itself is attractive and non-descript, resembling a tabletop lamp and breaking away from the usual pan/tilt form factor. It’s great for renters because you don’t have to mount it on a wall (although you can if that’s an option). It also supports AI video search and, with built-in storage, can continue recording during Wi-Fi outages.
Good for renters: LG Outdoor Cam

The LG Outdoor Cam from the Apple Home Collection can work for renters since it’s a plug-in camera; there’s no need to hardwire or replace existing light fixtures, as you have to with the Floodlight Cam.
The Outdoor Cam Plug-in supports 2.5K resolution, color and IR night vision, detection of people, pets, packages, and vehicles, person recognition, and AI-powered video search and descriptions.

This camera can be set up as a bullet camera or tilted downward at an angle. Like Eufy and Reolink cameras, the LG Outdoor Cam can record without Wi-Fi, ensuring you don’t lose important features when the Wi-Fi is out.

At $300, the LG Outdoor Cam follows the same pricing pattern as the rest of the Apple Home Collection. There are more affordable options, however, including the $60 Tapo MagCam and the Blink Outdoor 4, both of which are battery-powered for easier installation in rental properties.
Not so great for renters

Some of the products below aren’t ideal for most renters unless your lease terms are somewhat flexible. If you can get creative with setups, you could still use most of these products in a rental property, but I strongly suggest checking your lease before any installations.

I’ve compiled the remaining Apple Home Collection products with information on what makes them stand out, as well as pricing data, for whom they’re best suited, why they may not be ideal for renters, and some renter-friendly alternatives:
FAQ
Who is Apple’s target audience for the Home Collection?

Apple is appealing to loyalists with its Home Collection. The people who’ve already invested in the Apple ecosystem are the ones Apple wants to buy the Home Collection from. If you already own an iPhone, Apple Watch, HomePod, or an Apple TV device, you can manage new accessories from the same app without downloading a third-party application.
How secure are Apple’s smart home devices?

Apple is ensuring that most AI runs on-device for its new smart home products and that, if this isn’t possible, data goes only through Private Cloud Compute. Apple ensures the company cannot access your footage and emphasizes end-to-end encryption, as well as physical privacy features like those of the LG Indoor Cam.

With HomeKit Secure Video (HKSV), users enjoy intelligent detection, facial recognition, 10 days of recording history with an iCloud+ subscription (though this doesn’t count toward your storage capacity), Apple Home integration with Siri AI descriptions, and local video analysis.
What cameras are compatible with HKSV?

All new LG cameras in the Apple Home Collection are compatible with HKSV, but older cameras also support it. HKSV isn’t new or exclusive to the LG cameras. You can also use it with certain Aqara, Eve, Logitech, Eufy, and Netatmo cameras.

body: Social Security benefits to get a boost. And, Hasan Piker defends his rhetoric
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
Today's top stories

Consumer prices in September were 3.7% higher than they were a year ago, according to a Labor Department report. A spike in energy prices linked to the U.S. war with Iran drove up the cost of living. Excluding energy and food prices, core inflation reached 2.6% in September, up from August. The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% increase in benefits for next year after the release of the inflation report. This annual cost-of-living adjustment is based on prices from July, August and September. Some recipients say the increase is not enough.
- 🎧 Social Security may run out of money to make full payments to retirees as soon as 2032. NPR's Planet Money examines possible solutions.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced he will resume attacks on Russian oil refineries, despite President Trump's request to refrain from doing so. Zelenskyy told the Financial Times that he had ordered commanders to stand down earlier this week, but wouldn't anymore. But Ukraine's ability to conduct these long-range attacks may be limited, as it has seen sudden crippling restrictions to Starshield, the satellite communications system provided by the U.S.

- 🎧 The U.S. is seemingly trying to limit Ukraine's ability to fight Russia, though that has not been announced outright, NPR's Greg Myre tells Up First. Ukraine's defense ministry said today that operations are back to normal. The country relies on the Starshield system for offensive and defensive drones to protect against Russian strikes. Elon Musk, who developed the system for the U.S. government and military, says the U.S. government sets its speed and usage limits.

A man shot and wounded by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in New York last week says he didn't know the men who shot him were ICE agents until after he woke up in the hospital. A new petition filed in Brooklyn federal court says the agents — many of them masked — didn't identify themselves before approaching Oscar Belgal's vehicle with their firearms drawn. articles.headline: Trump Awkwardly Revisits Old Beef With Obama, And It’s Not What You Might Think
keyFacts: President Donald Trump questioned Barack Obama's Ivy League admission legitimacy during an Arizona rally.
Trump claimed Obama was not a smart guy and got into college for different reasons than others.
Obama previously earned degrees from Columbia University and graduated magna cum laude from Harvard Law School.
body: President Donald Trump on Wednesday revived a long-ago crusade against Barack Obama ― but it wasn’t about the former president’s place of birth.
This one questioned the legitimacy of Obama’s acceptance by Ivy League schools.
Trump told a rally crowd in Arizona that Obama “got into college for different reasons than you did.”
The president continued, “He’s not a smart guy.”

Trump again declared himself a “genius” in a rambling revisiting of his self-proclaimed cognitive-test triumphs. The president also expressed anger that he wasn’t praised for his claims before launching his attack on Obama.
Trump’s insecure beef with the higher education of the still-popular, two-term, non-impeached, non-convicted commander-in-chief dates way back.
In 2011, Trump was mulling a Republican run for president when he questioned then-President Obama’s academic qualifications.

“I heard he was a terrible student, terrible,” Trump said back then. “How does a bad student go to Columbia and then to Harvard? I’m thinking about it, I’m certainly looking into it. Let him show his records.”

While Obama noted in a memoir that he was not always an academic star, he earned a degree in political science from Columbia University in 1983 (after transferring from Occidental College) and later graduated magna cum laude from Harvard Law School.
Trump, meanwhile, has repeatedly blared to the world how smart he thinks he is and constantly bragged about his undergraduate education from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania.

However, Trump’s college grades have remained a mystery, and he reportedly got special treatment from a Penn admissions official who went to school with Trump’s older brother Fred, according to a 2001 biography, “The Trumps.”
